name: Merritt Levi
life: “I still remember receiving the final receipt in a torn pink envelope.” People around the window at Night Shift Donuts know Merritt by a small Wednesday habit. Merritt knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I paid for the mirror in monthly installments and still have the last little receipt.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a mustard canvas overshirt and a replacement button a shade darker than the others. Merritt has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, with a long plait tucked inside the collar. Merritt looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry during a conversation.
personality: Merritt uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Merritt well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To keep the last mirror receipt with its owner.
family: Jonathan Lund is Merritt’s cousin raised in the same household. Merritt brings a spare shopping bag. Jonathan chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A closing hour*, Jonathan says, “I can run the place alone and the owner knows it.”
connections: Daryl Maciel. The last purchase receipt stays in the same envelope as the new wheel bearing.

reactions.situation: The mirror owner wants it back during a fitting
reactions.response: Merritt asks the two shops for enough time to finish the fitting in privacy.

reactions.situation: An unfamiliar person asks for directions but cannot read the street signs
reactions.response: Merritt draws the route by its turns and entrances and has the person show which turn comes first.
